_what: Synthetic Ruby block-parameter gate for #3905 (RUBY-03), following bench/ruby-gem-resolution: exact accuracy cells and fingerprints, with ratios as the only timing gates. Real capture emitter, real parse worker (dist/), real Ruby ScopeResolver and manifest loader; analyze, persistence and full-pipeline memory are outside this benchmark.
_triage: Shape and fingerprint failures are deterministic: inspect the corpus and the resolved edges, never rebaseline just to make CI green. The runner also fails, before any baseline comparison, when a method misses an expected CALLS edge or gains one the source never makes. For a timing failure, rerun on an idle machine and verify the report shows its profile (ci: 5 interleaved samples after 1 warmup; full: 15 after 2) before investigating a regression. Millisecond observations are context, not gates.
_shape_note: Exact counts are the workload FLOOR. small = 64 methods x 6 blocks, large = 256 x 6 (methods 4x), dense = 64 x 24 (blocks per method 4x; in `nested`, nesting depth 4x). One class with one method per file. Expected edges per method are computed from the binder rule, not read back from the graph: a block that rebinds `user` (`|user|`, `|user, i|`) gets no edge, `|x|` reaches the nearest `user` (the local `User` unless an enclosing block rebinds it), and the closing `user.save` reaches User#save. main misses that rule (128 wrong edges at 32 x 6 side by side), so this gate fails without #3905. The one `member-lookup-ambiguous` decline per method is identical on main.
_fingerprint_note: Hashes pin every relationship (endpoints, type, confidence, reason) and every decline (reason, file, name, position).
_scaling_note: Scaling ratios are (t_4n/t_n)/4: about 1 is linear, about 4 is quadratic. 1.5 (bench/scope-capture) on every ratio: at these sizes main is linear along all three axes.
_one_file_note: Not gated: on main, Ruby resolution is super-linear in the number of classes or methods in ONE file. With every class in one file (`--shape crowded`), 256 -> 2048 methods, resolution's fitted exponent is 1.60 (1.48-1.72) on main and 1.61 (1.52-1.70) with #3905, per-doubling ratios 2.8 -> 3.5 on both; in a profile at 2048 classes the time is in ruby/merge-bindings.ts and in findClassBindingInScope / lookupMatchingNameClaim (scope-resolution/scope/walkers.ts). #3905 changes neither, and its absolute time there is lower (1180 vs 1641 ms at 2048). The gated shapes therefore use one class per file.
_profiles_note: Two profiles share the shapes and every accuracy gate. CI (the default, and what --check runs in the benchmarks job): one process, one parse worker, every workload timed, min of 5 after 1 warmup, interleaved. --full: one child times every workload, min of 15 after 2 warmups, and each shape runs in a fresh child for its peak RSS. Wall times are in _measured_ci.
_negative_controls_note: Re-running the Ruby scope query over the enclosing method for every block scope (O(blocks^2) per method, a temporary edit of languages/ruby/captures.ts) fails nested_capture_block_scaling_ratio 2.242 > 1.5 in the CI profile (sibling 1.473), with unchanged fingerprints. Two lighter O(blocks^2) edits (a walk of the method per block; collecting every block's parameters per block) raised the block ratios but stayed under 1.5 with 3 blocks per method, where per-file overhead dominates; that is why the shapes carry 6 blocks per method. These are deliberate regressions, not baseline observations.

_measured_ci.environment: macOS arm64 / Node 24.16.0, 2026-11-13, shared host (load average 7-40 on 15 cores)

_measured_full.environment: macOS arm64 / Node 24.16.0, 2026-11-13, shared host (load average 7-40 on 15 cores)

_measured_note: Three CI-profile runs and one --full run. Scalar ratios and millisecond values are per-metric maxima across the runs of that profile (rounded). peak_rss_mib (--full only) is each --shape child's high-water mark after one worker parse and one resolution, worker thread included; context, not gated. Exact shapes and fingerprints were identical in all runs. The doubling sweep in the PR comment (methods 256 -> 4096, blocks and depth 3 -> 48, three rounds, main and head) was measured separately with --shape --reps 3 --warmup 1 and is part of neither profile.
_rebaselined_on_main: Rebased #3905 onto 14d5405a5 after #3903 and #3880 merged. All six workloads retain their capture groups, CALLS, relationship counts, and zero missing/unexpected edges. DART-11 now records receiver-type-unresolved/untyped-binder declines: sibling small/large/dense 640/2560/2560; nested small/large/dense 704/2816/3008. Only those recorded declines and their fingerprints change; the pre-existing member-lookup-ambiguous counts and all scaling budgets are unchanged. Measured scaling ratios range from 0.692 to 1.056, below 1.5.
